title: Yod Keret
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Kiddushin 16b, Rav Yosef said, “I see Yod Keret here.” The Arukh cites the explanation that this is the name of a sage, while Rashi explains it differently.

notes.text: The name abbreviated אר״י remains unresolved. Rashi “explains differently” contrasts interpretations; בע״א does not mean the other page-side here. A bounded check of Kiddushin 16a–b did not locate this wording.

The saved whole named Davidson Kiddushin 16b paragraph explicitly has Rav Yosef saying יוד קרת קא חזינא הכא. This supersedes the earlier failed joined-form lookup and supports expanding אר״י as Rav Yosef in this citation, not the older Yirmiyah guess. The Arukh’s sage-name interpretation and Rashi’s different interpretation remain Hyman’s report; uninspected commentary snippets are not admitted as full evidence. בע״א means differently here, not another page-side.

Kiddushin 16b names Rav Yosef, resolving the initials in the earlier note. Rashi explains the image as turning a small yod into a large city, a figure for lengthening a teaching needlessly. The Arukh gives this explanation and also quotes a Gaon who takes Yod Keret as a sage’s name. The later Hafla’ah proposes reading “city” for “sage.” Ritva gives Rav Yosef for Rashi’s reading and reports a different reading, Rabbah, from the Raavad, who takes Yod Keret as a person’s name.
